headline: Japan’s October CPI Rises 2.3%, With Fresh-Food-Excluding Measure at 2.2%
deck: The Bank of Japan says it will raise its policy rate and adjust accommodation in response to activity, prices and financial conditions.
body: Japan’s Statistics Bureau reported that the all-items consumer price index in October was 2.3% higher than a year earlier, while the index excluding fresh food was 2.2% higher. [E1]
The paper’s 9 October Japan coverage was a household-spending survey for August; this is a new national price print for October. [E2]
The Bank of Japan says underlying CPI inflation is generally consistent with its 2% price-stability target. [E3]
Its October outlook says the Bank will continue to raise its policy rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in response to economic activity, prices and financial conditions. [E4]

evidence_box.fragment: Japan’s Statistics Bureau released October CPI on November 20: the all-items index was 2.3% higher than a year earlier, CPI excluding fresh food was 2.2% higher, and CPI excluding both fresh food and energy was also 2.2% higher.
